subject.title: [Feature]: Cloud Relay — openclaw login + heartbeat + relay for remote mobile access

question: Should OpenClaw core own an OAuth cloud relay, heartbeat, and mobile Gateway relay contract, and what trust/config model should govern it?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent and useful, but adding it would create new remote ingress, persistent credentials, backend ownership, config migration, and mobile trust commitments that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design core relay first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor, approve the trust/config/storage model, then split implementation into small Gateway, CLI, mobile, and backend-contract PRs.

options.title: Limit core to extension seams
options.body: Approve only missing plugin/API seams in core and require the hosted relay/backend implementation to live outside OpenClaw core until maintainers sponsor it.

options.title: Defer cloud relay
options.body: Reject or defer the relay direction for now and improve Tailscale, SSH, LAN, and QR/setup-code UX without adding cloud credentials or backend relay ownership.

recommendation.title: Design core relay first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor, approve the trust/config/storage model, then split implementation into small Gateway, CLI, mobile, and backend-contract PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history signal is on Gateway remote access, mobile setup-code routing, and the adjacent iOS pairing surfaces that this decision would change.
